r1_c3.reason: The core of this case is a tie argument: grant[arb] plus in_req[another] gives ranks[arb] <= ranks[another] (chosen_priority is the min over requesters), so the assertion needs strictness, i.e. ranks[arb] != ranks[another] plus arbitrary_requester != another_arbitrary_requester. With both indices dynamic, IC3 must discover the whole dynamic pairwise-distinctness family (the 120-clause permutation invariant), which is why frames blow up. For a fixed index k the needed fact reduces to the static conjunction 'ranks_k != ranks_j for all j!=k', and each such pairwise inequality is 1-inductive for this update (v->15 if v==cp, v-1 if v>cp, v otherwise is injective), so it is learnable. Fixing arbitrary_requester to a constant also collapses the heavy dynamic selects ranks[arb]/o_grant_vec_ref[arb] to single registers. No abstraction is applied: havocking any rank/rank_raw or chosen_priority only adds behaviours (arbitrary rank relations) and would turn this into a spurious SAT, since the property depends on the concrete permutation invariant.
